Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The bug occurs because when CSVFormat is created by newFormat(';') and other configurations, the recordSeparator property is null (see constructor CSVFormat(char,...,String recordSeparator,...) where recordSeparator is set to null by default). The CSVFormat.format method calls CSVPrinter.printRecord which finally calls CSVPrinter.println. The println method appends the recordSeparator string via out.append(recordSeparator), without checking if recordSeparator is null. Since recordSeparator is null, "null" string is appended to the output, causing the output to end with "null" instead of a newline or nothing.

The test expects the output not to end with "null" but since recordSeparator==null, "null" is appended by println(). The root cause is the lack of a default or fallback value for the recordSeparator string or a null check in CSVPrinter.println().

In summary:
- CSVFormat.recordSeparator is not initialized (null)
- CSVPrinter.println appends recordSeparator without null check
- CSVFormat.format uses CSVPrinter resulting in "null" string appended
- The test expects no "null" string appended, test fails.

This diagnosis matches the issue report: format always appends "null" (actually the string "null" that comes from appending null to StringWriter).

The likely fix is either initializing recordSeparator to a reasonable default or adding a null check before appending recordSeparator in CSVPrinter.println() to avoid appending "null".
